verdict.rationale: Fly.io documents its own sandbox capability: Sprites give each agent its own hardware-isolated, egress-locked, disposable Linux VM with a clean baseline per request and checkpoint rollback. That is genuine sandbox isolation for agent work, not a dry-run. The evidence does not show a test mode or staging environment explicitly separated from production data, and staging/production splits appear only as user-side arrangements. missing for 10: documented test/staging environment separated from production data, guidance on seeding or cloning non-production data, independent hands-on corroboration of Sprite isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Every agent gets its own Linux box.
Run it in a hardware-isolated VM. A clean baseline per request, so no two users ever share state. Egress-locked and disposable.
Roll back to any checkpoint in seconds
Grant access on purpose: by Sprite name, by label, or down to a single endpoint, so a Slack bot can post messages and never touch admin.
